title: QProfile crosswalk: latency vs accuracy sensitivity sweep (FP16 / INT8 / INT4)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a cross-profile sensitivity sweep to map latency (tokens/sec, p95) and quality regressions across FP16, INT8 and INT4 builds for representative production workloads. This ticket builds a reusable harness that: (1) runs mixed-sequence-length traffic patterns, (2) exercises KV-cache priming and long-context flows, (3) measures tokens/sec and p95 tail latency per model/profile, and (4) computes quality deltas on a sampled evaluation set (mix of summarization, instruction, and QA prompts). The goal is to produce a deployable profile matrix and regression gating rules so the Console/Optimize tooling can recommend safe quantization levels per workload. This differs from prior brute-force sweeps by adding SLA-aware routing scenarios (e.g., fall back to FP16 for p95 > threshold) and a statistical regression detector (EWMA + change-point) so we can flag subtle drops in quality or latency early.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can execute automated sweeps for FP16, INT8, INT4 across at least 3 model families and report tokens/sec and p95 per profile
Quality evaluation computed for each profile on the canonical eval set with diff vs FP16 baseline (ROUGE-L and answer-accuracy) and stored as time-series
Regression detector (EWMA + change point) implemented and generates alerts when quality delta > 2% absolute or p95 increases > 30% vs baseline
Runbook created describing safe fallback thresholds and how Console/Optimize will consume the matrix
PR with the harness code merged and integration job added to CI (nightly sweep), and dashboard seeded with first sweep results
steps: Create harness wrapper around existing load-runner: tools/load-runner --model <model> --profile <fp16|int8|int4> --seq-distribution <short|mixed|long> --warmup=200 --duration=30m
Define seq-distribution mixes: short(0-128)=50%, medium(128-512)=35%, long(512-2048)=15%
KV cache priming: run priming workload for each model/profile before measurement window to stabilize KV hit rate
Collect metrics: tokens/sec (aggregate and per-second), latency p50/p90/p95/p99, GPU util, memory, and tail CPU stalls
Quality eval: run sampled inference on eval set (n=1200 prompts), compute ROUGE-L for summarization, exact-match/accuracy for QA, and store diffs vs FP16 baseline
Regression detection: compute EWMA on quality and p95, run CUSUM change-point to detect sustained shifts, emit 'regression' when thresholds breached
Dashboards: populate a per-model profile matrix and time-series panels; add an alert rule to detect repeated regressions over 3 runs
notes: Initial small-scale runs (3 models, region eu-west-1) show INT8 improves tokens/sec by ~1.7x on average with a median p95 uplift of 18% over FP16 for mixed sequences
INT4 runs show the biggest variance: when long-context >1024 tokens p95 spikes 2-3x and quality (ROUGE-L) drops 3-6% on summarization set; for short sequences INT4 is competitive

Observed hotspot: INT4 kernel path suffers cache-thrashing on batches with mixed sequence lengths. Hypothesis: microbatch scheduling + KV cache eviction policies amplify tail latency under mixed workloads
Decision: add an explicit path in harness to measure 'context-sensitive' SLOs and tag problematic runs so Optimize can recommend 'INT4 for short-seq only'
We must confirm hardware-specific behavior: schedule a cross-GPU sweep on A100, H100 and an AMD MI300 node (availability permitting) to ensure matrix portability
Blocker: flaky gating tests in CI due to shared cluster noise. Short-term mitigation: run nightly on a reserved dedicated pool (small token cost) to reduce variance
